findings.question: q-biology-evolution-0004
findings.quote: Some insects already carry a heritable pesticide-resistance variant. Spraying leaves these insects with more surviving offspring on average. Why does resistance become common?
findings.problem: The stem supplies the keyed answer before asking for it. A student can match “more surviving offspring” to “Resistant insects leave more descendants” without explaining how natural selection changes a population.
findings.fix: Describe the resistant insects surviving spraying more often, then ask why resistance increases over generations; make the key connect inherited resistance with greater reproductive success.

findings.question: q-biology-evolution-0014
findings.quote: Divergence may lead to reproductive isolation.
findings.problem: The stem asks which outcome is “possible,” and the key is the only choice phrased as a possibility (“may”). All distractors assert categorical guarantees or prohibitions (“guarantees immediate,” “prevents any,” and “stops until”). A student can choose the only tentative statement by wording alone without understanding speciation.
findings.fix: Phrase every choice as a possible outcome and use plausible competing predictions about gene flow, divergence, and interbreeding.
